finding.claim: The authenticated identity is read directly from a client-supplied HTTP header (X-Session-User-Verified). Nothing in this code verifies a session, signature or token, so any client that can reach the app can impersonate any user named in a resource's grants. This is exploitable unless an upstream proxy strips and overwrites the header, which the code does not enforce.
finding.source: Attacker-controlled request header X-Session-User-Verified. Precondition: the attacker reaches the app directly, or the fronting proxy does not strip or overwrite the header. The attacker also needs to know or guess a grantee's user name.
finding.sink: Protected operations: DELETE /files/<fid> (del STORE[fid]) and POST /files/<fid>/rename (f["name"] = ...), both authorized only by is_allowed(g.user, ...).

trace.note: g.user = request.headers.get('X-Session-User-Verified') is taken verbatim from the request
ensure_allowed(g.user, f, 'delete') authorizes the delete with the spoofed identity
is_allowed only checks action in grants.get(user, []), so a spoofed name that has a grant passes
del STORE[fid] runs, deleting the file
The rename route uses the same spoofed g.user for its write check
f['name'] is overwritten with attacker-supplied data

finding.guards_checked: Searched the two files for session, signature, token or proxy-trust checks and found none. The header name implies an upstream proxy verifies it, but nothing here confirms that or rejects direct requests. The ACL itself is correct for a missing user: g.user None gets no grants and a 403. Other issues are not exploitable security flaws: STORE[fid] raises KeyError (a 500 on unknown ids) and request.json['name'] is unvalidated, which only causes errors.

verdict.guard_found: ensure_allowed (acl.py:8-10) aborts 403 and its result is used correctly; is_allowed (views.py:25) is tested. Neither authenticates the header. No session, signature or proxy-trust check in the code.
verdict.reason: Every trace line is accurate (views.py:11 reads the header verbatim, views.py:17/25 authorize with it, acl.py:5 only checks grants), and no in-code control authenticates it. Whether an upstream proxy strips and sets X-Session-User-Verified is deployment-specific and not visible in these two files, so exploitability can't be decided from the code.
